Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Yunus (Jonah), because it uniquely mentions the story of the people of the Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him), and what happened with their faith after the threat of the descent of the punishment, which Allah removed from them.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Establishing the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ) by the evidence of the inability of the polytheists to produce the like of the Qur'an, and clarifying that the Qur'an is from Allah; mentioning the stance of the polytheists regarding the reality of the message and the Qur'an; refuting their denial that Allah would send a messenger from among mankind; and reminding them of what befell the people of the past centuries when they associated partners with Allah and denied the messengers.

• Establishing that Allah, the Exalted, is alone in divinity by the evidence of His lordship, since He is the Creator of the world and its Manager. This leads to refuting that Allah has partners in His divinity, and refuting the excuses of the polytheists that their idols are intercessors with Allah.

• Establishing the resurrection and the recompense, clarifying the wisdom and nature of the recompense, warning those who deny the resurrection and turn away from the signs of Allah, and rebuking the polytheists for what they forbade of what Allah had made lawful.

• Mentioning the stories of some prophets with their peoples, and mentioning the stance of their peoples in denying them, which is similar to the situation of the disbelievers with the Prophet (ﷺ); urging reflection on what befell them as the recompense for their denial, and consoling the small believing group by mentioning the end of the believers who had faith in their prophets.

• Citing the testimony of the People of the Book as evidence for the truthfulness of the Prophet's message.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾. The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah, the letters that open some surahs) has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. These are the verses of the Book (al-Kitab), the perfectly firm one, which Allah made firm and clarified for His servants.

Was it a strange matter for people that We sent down the revelation with the Qur'an to a man from among them, to warn them of God's punishment and to give good tidings to those who believed in God and His messengers that they will have a good reward for the righteous deeds they had sent forward? When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to them with God's revelation and recited it to them, the deniers said: "Muhammad is a sorcerer, and what he brought is clearly manifest sorcery."

Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days. Then He established Himself (istawa), that is: He rose above and ascended, upon the Throne, in a manner that befits His majesty and His greatness. He manages the affairs of His creation; none opposes His decree, and no intercessor intercedes with Him on the Day of Resurrection except after He has given him permission to intercede. So worship Allah, your Lord, who is characterized by these attributes, and devote your worship sincerely to Him. Will you not then take heed and learn a lesson from these signs and proofs?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 4:

To Allah is your return on the Day of Resurrection, all of you together. This is the true promise of Allah. It is He who begins the creation and then repeats it after death, returning them alive in their former form, in order to reward with the best reward, in justice, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger and performed good deeds. As for those who denied the oneness of Allah and the message of His Messenger, they will have a drink of boiling water that scalds the faces and tears apart the intestines, and they will have a painful punishment because of their disbelief and misguidance.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 10, verse 5:**

Allah is the One who made the sun a source of radiance, and made the moon a light, and determined for it phases, so that by the sun the days are known, and by the moon the months and years are known. Allah the Exalted did not create the sun and the moon except for a great wisdom, and as a sign of the perfection of Allah's power and knowledge. He makes clear the proofs and evidences for a people who understand the wisdom in the origination of creation.

In the alternation of night and day, and in what God has created in the heavens and the earth of marvels of creation and of artistry and order within them, there are indeed clear signs and proofs for a people who fear God's punishment, His wrath, and His chastisement.

Indeed, those who do not hope to meet Us [for reckoning] in the Hereafter, and for the recompense for their deeds that follows it, because they deny the Resurrection; and who are content with the worldly life in place of the Hereafter and rely upon it; and those who are heedless of Our signs, both the cosmic and the legislated.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 8:

Those—their abode is the Fire of Hell in the Hereafter, as recompense for what they used to earn in their worldly life of sins and transgressions.

Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them to the path of Paradise, and will grant them success in the deeds that lead to it, because of their faith. Then He will reward them by entering Paradise and by bestowing His good pleasure upon them. Rivers will flow beneath their mansions and dwellings in the Gardens of Bliss.

Their supplication in Paradise will be glorification (of God): "Glory be to You, O God" (subhanaka Allahumma). Their greeting from God and His angels will be (salam), and they will greet one another with (salam) in Paradise. The last of their supplications will be their saying: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds," meaning: thanks and praise belong to God, the Creator of all creatures and their Sustainer through His blessings.

"If Allah were to hasten to people the granting of their supplications for evil, as He hastens to grant them what is good, they would have been destroyed. So We leave those who do not fear Our punishment, and do not believe with certainty in the Resurrection and the Rising, to wander bewildered in their rebellion and their arrogance."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 12:

When hardship befalls the human being, he calls upon Us to relieve him of it, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing, according to the state he is in when that harm descends upon him. But when We relieve him of the hardship that had befallen him, he carries on in his former way, as before the harm reached him, forgetting the hardship and affliction he had been in, and neglecting to give thanks to his Lord who relieved him of the affliction that had descended upon him. Just as this human being was made to see as fair his persistence in his denial and obstinacy after God removed from him the harm he was in, so too were those who committed excess in lying against God and His prophets made to see as fair the acts of disobedience to God and the associating of partners with Him that they used to do.

This is a verse-by-verse commentary, so I translate the passage as it stands.

The commentary on surah 10, verse 13 (King Fahd Complex, al-Tafsir al-Muyassar):

We had already destroyed the nations before you, O idolaters, who denied the messengers of God, when they committed shirk (associating partners with their Lord). Their messengers came to them from God with clear miracles and proofs that showed the truthfulness of those who brought them. But those nations whom We destroyed were not going to believe their messengers or submit to them, so they deserved destruction. In this way, We recompense every criminal who transgresses the limits of God.

Then We made you, O people, successors in the earth after the generations that were destroyed, so that We might see how you would act: whether good or evil, and We would then reward you according to your deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 15:

When Our clear verses are recited to the polytheists, those who do not fear the Reckoning, do not hope for reward, and do not believe in the Day of Resurrection and Gathering say: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it.﴾ That is, [say to him, O Messenger]: "Make the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful, turn the promise into a threat and the threat into a promise, and remove from it what censures our gods and what makes our minds seem foolish."

Say to them, O Messenger: "That is not up to me. I only follow in everything I command you or forbid you of what my Lord sends down to me and orders me to do. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey His command, the punishment of a great Day, which is the Day of Resurrection."

Say, [O Messenger]: "Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would God have made you aware of it. So know that it is the truth from God, for you know that I lived among you for a long time before He sent it down to me, and before I recited it to you. Will you not then use your reason through reflection and contemplation?"

No one does greater wrong than the one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs. Indeed, whoever denies the prophets and messengers of Allah will not succeed, and they will not attain prosperity.

The polytheists worship, besides God, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them, in this world or the next, and they say: "We only worship them so that they may intercede for us with God." Say to them, O Messenger: "Will you inform God of something He does not know, concerning these intercessors, in the heavens or on the earth?" For if there were intercessors in them who would intercede for you with Him, He would have more knowledge of them than you do. Exalted is God above what these polytheists do in associating with Him in His worship that which neither harms nor benefits.

People were once upon one religion, which is Islam. Then they differed after that: some of them disbelieved, and some of them remained steadfast upon the truth. Had it not been for a word that preceded from Allah, granting respite to the disobedient and not hastening their punishment for their sins, the matter would have been decided between them: that the people of falsehood among them would be destroyed, and the people of truth would be saved.

These disbelieving, obstinate people say: "Why has no sign (ayah) been sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, a tangible proof by which we would know that he is right in what he says?" So say to them, O Messenger: "The Unseen (al-ghayb) is known to no one but Allah. If He wills, He does it, and if He wills, He does not do it. So wait, O people, for Allah's judgment between us and you, by hastening His punishment upon the one of us who is in falsehood, and granting victory to the one who holds the truth. Indeed, I am waiting for that along with you."

And when We let the disbelievers taste ease and relief and comfort after hardship and distress had befallen them, behold, they begin to deny and mock Our signs. Say, [O Messenger], to these mocking disbelievers: Allah is swifter in plotting, in gradual seizing, and in punishment against you. Indeed, Our recording angels, whom We send to you, write down what you plot against Our signs; then We will call you to account for that.

He is the One who enables you to travel, [O people], on land by means of animals and other conveyances, and at sea in ships. When you are in the ships and they sail with a good wind, and the passengers rejoice in the favorable wind, a violent wind comes upon the ships, and the waves (that is, water that has risen up) come upon the passengers from every direction. They become certain that destruction has encompassed them, so they sincerely direct their supplication to Allah alone, and abandon what they used to worship. They say: "If You deliver us from this distress we are in, we will surely be among those who give thanks to You for Your blessings."

So when Allah rescued them from the hardships and terrors, behold, they went right back to spreading corruption on the earth and committing sins. "O mankind, your transgression only recoils upon yourselves. You enjoy it as a fleeting pleasure in this worldly life, which passes away. Then to Us is your return and your final destination, and We will inform you of all your deeds and call you to account for them."

The likeness of the life of this world is only like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, from which men and animals eat; until, when the earth takes on its adornment and becomes beautiful, and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it a harvest, as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain the signs for a people who reflect.

Note: the passage given is the tafsir commentary itself, and my rendering above reproduces the Qur'anic verse rather than the commentary's prose. Here is the full translation of the commentary as requested:

The likeness of the worldly life, and of what you boast of in it of adornment and wealth, is like rain which We sent down from the sky to the earth, so that by it there sprouted varieties of vegetation, intermingled with one another, of what people feed on, such as fruits, and what animals eat of plants. Until, when the beauty and splendour of this earth became manifest, and the people of this earth thought that they were able to harvest it and benefit from it, there came to it Our command and decree of destruction upon what was on it of vegetation and adornment, whether by night or by day. So We made these plants and trees reaped and cut down, with nothing left in them, as if those crops and plants had not been standing on the face of the earth before that. Thus does ruin come upon what you boast of in your worldly life and its ornaments; God will annihilate and destroy it. And just as We have shown you, O people, the likeness of this world and made you know its reality, We make Our proofs and signs clear to a people who reflect upon the signs of God and ponder what benefits them in this world and the Hereafter.
And Allah calls you to His Gardens, which He has prepared for His allies, and He guides whomever He wills of His creation, granting him success in reaching the straight path, which is Islam.

For the believers who did good (in their worship of Allah) by obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade, there is the Garden, and an increase upon it, which is beholding the Face of Allah, the Exalted, in the Garden; and forgiveness and pleasure (from Allah). Dust will not cover their faces, nor humiliation, as will befall the people of the Fire. Those who possess these attributes are the companions of the Garden, abiding therein forever.

The Noble Qur'an verse is quoted within the commentary; the passage is a gloss, so I translate it as it stands.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 27:

Those who committed evil deeds in the world, disbelieved, and disobeyed Allah, will receive a recompense for their evil deeds equal to them, from the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. Humiliation and disgrace will cover them, and they will have no protector from the punishment of Allah when He punishes them. It is as if their faces had been clothed with pieces of the dark black of the night. These are the people of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.

Remember, O Messenger, the Day when We gather all of creation for reckoning and recompense. Then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your places, you and your partners whom you used to worship besides Allah, until you see what will be done with you." Then We will separate the polytheists from those they worshipped, and those who were worshipped besides Allah will disown those who used to worship them, and they will say to the polytheists: "You did not worship us in the world."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 29:

"Then God is sufficient as a witness between us and you. Indeed, we did not know what you used to say and do, and we were truly unaware of your worship of us; we were not aware of it."

In that standing for reckoning, every soul will examine its past conditions and deeds and witness them, and will be recompensed according to them: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil. All will be returned to Allah, the just Judge, so the people of Paradise will be admitted to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, and what the polytheists used to worship besides Allah will vanish from them, having been fabrications against Him.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: Who provides for you from the heaven, by sending down rain, and from the earth, by causing to grow in it various kinds of plants and trees, of which you and your livestock eat? Who possesses hearing and sight, the senses through which you and others enjoy benefits? And who controls life and death throughout the whole universe, bringing forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living, among the creatures you know and among those you do not know? Who directs the affair of the heaven and the earth and whatever is in them, and your affair and the affair of all creation? They will surely answer you that the One who does all of that is Allah. So say to them: Will you not fear the punishment of Allah if you worship others alongside Him?

That is Allah, your true Lord, the Truth about whom there is no doubt, the One deserving of worship alone, with no partner. So what lies beyond the truth except error? How, then, are you turned away from worshipping Him to worship other than Him?

Just as these polytheists disbelieved and persisted in their polytheism, the word of your Lord, His decree and His judgment, has come into effect against those who turned away from obedience to their Lord towards disobedience to Him and disbelieved in Him: that they do not affirm the Oneness of God, nor the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and do not act upon his guidance.

Say, [O Messenger]: "Is there any of your associate-deities who originates creation from nothing, then causes it to perish after its bringing into being, and then restores it to its form before it perished?" Indeed, they are unable to claim that. Say, [O Messenger]: "It is Allah, alone, who originates creation, then causes it to perish, then restores it. So how are you turned away from the path of truth to falsehood, which is the worship of other than Allah?"

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: "Is there any among your partners who guides to the straight path?" Indeed, they are unable to do that. Say to them: "Allah alone guides the one who has strayed from guidance to the truth. Which of the two is more worthy of being followed: He who guides alone to the truth, or the one who does not find guidance, due to his lack of knowledge and his misguidance, and they are your partners who neither guide nor are guided unless they are guided?" So what is the matter with you, how do you equate Allah with His creation? And this is a false judgment.

Most of these polytheists follow nothing but conjecture and guesswork in making idols into gods and believing that they bring them closer to Allah. Conjecture does not avail anything against certainty. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what these polytheists do of disbelief and denial.

It was not possible for anyone to bring this Qur'an from other than God, because no one among creation is able to do that. Rather, God sent it down as a confirmation of the Books that He sent down to His prophets, because the religion of God is one. In this Qur'an is clarification and elaboration of what God legislated for the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). There is no doubt that this Qur'an is revealed from the Lord of the worlds.

Rather, do they say, "He [Muhammad] has invented it himself"? Say: "Then bring forth a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."

Actually, they say: "He invented it." Say, [O Messenger]: "Then produce one surah of the same kind as this Qur'an in its arrangement and its guidance, and seek help in that from everyone you are able to muster besides Allah, of mankind and the jinn, if you are truthful in your claim."

Rather, they hastened to deny the Qur'an the moment they heard it, before they had reflected on its verses, and they disbelieved in what they had not encompassed in knowledge: the mention of the Resurrection, the recompense, Paradise, the Fire, and other things besides. And the reality of what they were promised in the Book has not yet come to them. Just as the polytheists denied Allah's threat, the nations that passed away before them also denied, so look, O Messenger, at how the end of the wrongdoers was: Allah destroyed some of them by sinking into the earth, some of them by drowning, and some of them by other means.

Among your people, O Messenger, are some who believe in the Qur'an, and among them are some who do not believe in it, and they will die upon that and be raised upon it. Your Lord knows best the corrupters who do not believe in it, out of wrongdoing, obstinacy and corruption, and He will requite them for their corruption with the most severe punishment.

And if these polytheists deny you, O Messenger, then say to them: "For me is my religion and my deed, and for you is your religion and your deed. You will not be held accountable for my deed, and I will not be held accountable for your deeds."

Among the disbelievers are those who listen to your words of truth and to your recitation of the Qur'an, but they will not be guided. Can you then make the deaf hear? Likewise, you cannot guide these people unless God wills their guidance, because they are deaf to hearing the truth and do not understand it.

Among the disbelievers there are those who look at you and at the clear proofs of your prophethood, but they do not perceive the light of faith that God has given you. Will you, O Messenger, be able to make the blind see, so that they may be guided by their sight? Likewise, you cannot guide them when they are bereft of insight; all of that belongs to God alone.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 44:

Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, by adding to their misdeeds or diminishing from their good deeds. But it is people who wrong themselves, through disbelief, disobedience, and opposing the command and prohibition of Allah.

On the Day He gathers these polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection and Reckoning, it will be as though they had not remained in the worldly life except for an hour of the day. They will recognize one another as they did in the world; then that recognition will cease and that hour will have passed. Those who disbelieved and denied the meeting with Allah, His reward and His punishment, have certainly lost, and they were not guided to what is right in what they did.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 46:

Whether We show you (O Messenger) during your lifetime some of what We promise them of punishment in this world, or We cause you to die before We show you that happening to them, to Us alone they will return in both cases. Then Allah is Witness over their deeds that they used to do in the world; nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will requite them with the recompense they deserve.

And for every nation (ummah) that passed before you, O people, there was a messenger whom I sent to them, just as I sent Muhammad to you, calling to the religion of God and obedience to Him. So when their messenger comes on the Day of Judgment, judgment will then be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged in the least in the recompense for their deeds.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 48:

The disbelievers among your people, O Messenger, say: "When will the Hour arrive, if you and those who follow you are truthful about what you promise us?"

Say, [O Messenger], "I have no power to bring harm or benefit to myself, except as Allah wills. For every nation there is a term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by a single hour, nor can they advance it."
Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: Tell me, if God's punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals are hastening to bring about, the descent of the punishment?

Is it only after Allah's punishment has befallen you, O polytheists, that you believe, at a time when belief will not benefit you? And it will be said to you at that time: "Do you believe in it now, when you used to seek to hasten it?"

Then it will be said to those who wronged themselves by their disbelief in Allah: "Taste the eternal punishment of Allah, which is yours forever. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to do in your lives of disobedience to Allah?"

This is a translation of a Qur'anic commentary passage (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, from the King Fahd Complex), not a quotation of the verse itself. The commentary's gloss on verse 10:53 reads:

And these disbelievers from your people, O Messenger, ask you for information about the punishment on the Day of Resurrection: "Is it true?" Say to them, O Messenger: "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, without any doubt. And you cannot escape from Allah, so that He would not resurrect you and recompense you; for you are in His grasp and under His authority."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 54:

If every soul that committed shirk and disbelieved in Allah possessed everything on earth, and were able to offer it as a ransom to free itself from that punishment, it would surely offer it. And those who did wrong will conceal their remorse when they see the punishment of Allah standing over them all. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will judge between them with justice, and they will not be wronged, because Allah, exalted is He, does not punish anyone except for his own sin.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 55:

Unquestionably, everything in the heavens and everything on the earth belongs to Allah, the Exalted; none of that belongs to anyone other than Him. Unquestionably, the meeting with Allah the Exalted and His punishment for the polytheists are certain to occur, but most of them do not know the reality of that.

Indeed, Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. It is not difficult for Him to bring people back to life after they die, just as He is not unable to cause them to die when He wills that. And they will all return to Him after their death.

O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord, reminding you of the punishment of God and warning you of His threat. It is the Qur'an and what it contains of signs and admonitions, to reform your character and your deeds. In it is a cure for what is in the hearts of ignorance, polytheism (shirk) and all other diseases, and guidance for whoever follows it among creation, saving him from destruction. He, glory be to Him and exalted, made it a blessing and a mercy for the believers, and specified them with it, because they are the ones who benefit from faith. As for the disbelievers, it is for them a blindness.

Say, [O Messenger], to all of mankind: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, and that is what has come to them from Allah of guidance and the religion of truth, which is Islam. So in that let them rejoice; for Islam, to which Allah has called them, and the Qur'an which He sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), are better than what they amass of the worldly goods and what is in it of fleeting, perishing adornment."

Say, [O Messenger], to these deniers of the revelation: Tell me about this provision which Allah has created for you from livestock, plants and good things, and you have made some of it lawful for yourselves and forbidden some of it. Say to them: Has Allah permitted you to do that, or do you attribute to Allah what is false and lie?

And what do those think, who fabricate lies against Allah, about the Day of Reckoning? They add to Him the prohibition of what He did not prohibit for them of provisions and sustenance. Do they suppose that Allah will do with them on the Day of Resurrection what they deserve for their lying and their fabrication against Him? Do they suppose that He will overlook them and forgive them? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward His creation, by leaving off hastening the punishment of one who fabricates lies against Him in this world and by granting him respite. But most people do not thank Allah for His bounty toward them in this.

And you (O Messenger) are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite any part of the Qur'an, nor do any of you (the people of this Ummah) do any deed, whether good or bad, except that We are witnesses over you, observing it as you undertake it and carry it out. We preserve it for you and will recompense you for it. And nothing escapes the knowledge of your Lord, O Messenger, of even the weight of a small ant in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller or greater than that, except that it is in a clear and manifest Book with Allah, His knowledge encompasses it and His pen has recorded it.

Note: this passage is a paraphrase of Q. 10:62, which is rendered below.

Indeed, the friends of Allah (awliya' Allah) will have no fear in the Hereafter of Allah's punishment, nor will they grieve over what they missed of the pleasures of this world.

The attributes of these awliya' (close friends of God) are that they are those who believed in Allah, followed His Messenger, and what he brought from Allah, and who used to fear Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

For these friends of Allah there is good news from Allah in the worldly life, of what gladdens them, among which is the righteous dream that the believer sees or that is seen for him; and in the Hereafter, (there is good news of) Paradise. Allah does not break His promise, nor does He change it. That is the great triumph, because it includes deliverance from every harm and attainment of every desired and beloved thing.

Do not let their words grieve you, O Messenger: the words of the polytheists about their Lord, their fabrications against Him, and their association with Him of idols and images. For Allah, exalted is He, is the One who alone possesses complete power and perfect might, in this world and in the Hereafter. He is the All-Hearing of their sayings and the All-Knowing of their intentions and deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 66:

Surely, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, from the angels, mankind, the jinn, and others besides them. And what do those who call upon other than Allah, the partners, follow? They follow only conjecture, and they are only lying in what they attribute to Allah.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 10, verse 67:**

He is the One who made the night for you, O people, so that you may rest in it and be relieved from the toil of moving about in pursuit of livelihood. And He made the day for you so that you may see by it and strive to seek your provision. Indeed, in the alternation of night and day, and in the condition of their people within them, there are clear signs and proofs that Allah alone is deserving of worship, for a people who hear these proofs and reflect upon them.

The polytheists said: "Allah has taken a son," as their saying: "The angels are daughters of Allah," or "The Messiah is the son of Allah." Allah is exalted above all of that and far removed from it. He is the Self-Sufficient, free of need for anything other than Himself. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. How, then, could He have a son from among what He created, when everything is owned by Him? You have no proof for the lie you fabricate. Do you say about Allah what you do not know to be true?
Say: Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah, by ascribing a son to Him and attributing partners to Him, will not attain their aim, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 70:

They enjoy only a brief provision in this world because of their disbelief and their lying. Then, when their term has ended, their return is to Us. Then We will make them taste the punishment of Jahannam (Hell), because of their disbelief in Allah, their denial of Allah's messengers, and their rejection of His signs.

Recount to them, O Messenger, to the disbelievers of Makkah, the story of Nuh (peace be upon him) with his people, when he said to them: "If my standing among you and my reminding you of the proofs and evidences of Allah has become burdensome to you, then my reliance is upon Allah and my trust is in Him. So resolve upon your affair, and call upon your partners. Then do not let your affair be concealed from you, but let it be open and manifest. Then carry out your decision against me with the punishment and the harm that is within your power, and do not give me respite for an hour of a day."

If you turn away from my call, then I have not asked you for any wage, for my reward is with my Lord and my recompense is upon Him, the One who has no partner, and I have been commanded to be among those who submit to His judgment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 73:

Yet his people denied him regarding what he told them from Allah. So We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We made them successors in the earth, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So reflect, O Messenger, on how was the end of those people who were warned by their messenger of Allah's punishment and His might.

Then after Noah We sent messengers to their peoples (Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shu'ayb and others), and each messenger came to his people with miracles that proved his prophethood and the truth of what he called them to. Yet they were not going to believe and act upon what the earlier nations had denied, those who came before them. Just as Allah sealed the hearts of these peoples so that they did not believe, so too He seals the hearts of those who resemble them among those who came after them, who transgressed the bounds of Allah and opposed what their messengers called them to of obedience to Him, as a punishment for their sins.

Then after those messengers, We sent Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both, to Fir'awn and the nobles of his people, with miracles that proved their truthfulness. But they became arrogant and refused to accept the truth. They were a people who were polytheists, criminals, and deniers.
When Moses brought Pharaoh and his people the clear miracles he had been sent with, they said: "This is nothing but evident magic."

Moses said to them, expressing astonishment at their words: "Do you say of the truth, when it has come to you, that it is clear magic? Look at the description of what has come to you and what it contains, and you will find it to be the truth. The magicians do not prosper; they do not win, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter."

Pharaoh and his chiefs said to Musa: "Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers upon, the worship of other than Allah, and so that you and Harun may have greatness and dominion in the land of Egypt? We will not affirm for you both that you are two messengers sent to us, so that we may worship Allah alone, with no partner."
Pharaoh said: "Bring me every skilled sorcerer."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 80:**

When the sorcerers came to Pharaoh, Musa said to them: "Throw onto the ground whatever you have of your ropes and your staffs."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 81:

When they threw down their ropes and their staffs, Moses said to them: "What you have brought, and what you have thrown, is magic. Indeed, Allah will nullify it and render it void. Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of those who strive in the land of Allah with what He dislikes, and who spread corruption in it through their disobedience."

And Allah will establish the truth that I have brought you from Him, and make it prevail over your falsehood by His words and His command, even though the criminals, the people of sin from the family of Pharaoh, dislike it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 83:

Yet none believed in Musa (peace be upon him), despite the proofs and evidence that had come to them, except a small group (dhurriyyah) of his people from the Children of Israel, and they were fearful of Fir'awn and his chiefs lest they subject them to torment and turn them away from their religion. Indeed, Fir'awn was a tyrant, arrogant on the earth, and he was truly one of those who exceed the limits in disbelief and corruption.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 84:

And Musa said: "O my people, if you have believed in Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and have complied with His law, then place your trust in Him, and submit to His command, and rely upon Allah if you are submissive to Him in obedience."

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 85:

The people of Musa said to him: "In Allah alone, with no partner, do we place our trust, and to Him we have entrusted our affair. Our Lord, do not make them a trial for us, so that they would prevail over us and that would be a temptation for us away from the religion, or the disbelievers would be tempted by their victory, and say: 'Had they been upon the truth, they would not have been defeated.'"
And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people — Pharaoh and his chiefs — for they were subjecting them to hard labor.

And We revealed to Moses and his brother Aaron: "Settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses places of worship (qiblah), and establish the prayer. And give good tidings to the believers."

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given, not the verse alone. Here is the faithful translation:

And We revealed to Moses and his brother Aaron that they should settle houses for their people in "Egypt," which would serve as dwellings and shelters in which you seek refuge. And make your houses places where you pray during fear, and perform the prayer that has been prescribed at its appointed times. And give good tidings to the believers who obey Allah with decisive victory and abundant reward from Him, glorified and exalted be He.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 88:

And Moses said: "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and the nobles of his people adornment and wealth in the life of this world, and they have not given thanks to You for it. Rather, they have used it to help them lead people astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not be opened to faith and will not believe until they see the painful punishment."

God said to them both: "Your supplication has been answered concerning Pharaoh, his chiefs and their wealth." Moses was the one making supplication, while Aaron said "Amin" to his supplication; for this reason the supplication is attributed to both of them. "So remain steadfast upon your path, and continue calling Pharaoh and his people to the Oneness of God and obedience to Him, and do not follow the way of those who do not know the reality of My promise and My threat."

We made the Children of Israel cross the sea until they had passed through it. Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them, out of injustice and aggression. They entered the sea behind them, until, when drowning encompassed Pharaoh, he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am one of those who submit in obedience and surrender."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 91:

Now, O Pharaoh, when death has come upon you, do you acknowledge submission to God? Yet you disobeyed Him before His punishment descended upon you, and you were among the corrupters who turned others away from His path!! Repentance will not benefit you at the moment of death-agony and witnessing death and punishment.

Now today We shall save your body, that you may be a sign for those who come after you. Indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs and proofs; they do not reflect upon them nor take heed.

Wait, that rendering is not faithful to the Arabic. Here is the accurate translation:

So today We shall place you upon a high place of the earth with your body, so that those who denied your destruction may look upon you; that you may be a lesson for those after you among the people, by which they may take heed. And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our proofs and signs; they do not reflect upon them nor take heed.

This is a commentary on the Qur'an, so I'll render each Qur'anic quotation's meaning within ﴿ ﴾ markers.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 93:

We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good and chosen dwelling in the lands of "al-Sham" (Greater Syria) and "Misr" (Egypt), and We provided them with lawful and good sustenance from the blessed produce of the earth. Yet they did not differ concerning the matter of their religion except after the knowledge had come to them, the knowledge that required their unity and harmony. Among that knowledge was what the Torah contained concerning the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Indeed, your Lord, O Messenger, will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, and will decide concerning what they used to differ about regarding your matter, so He will admit the deniers into the Fire and the believers into Paradise.

If you, O Messenger, are in doubt about the truth of what We have told you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you, from among the People of the Torah and the Gospel, asking for confirmation and testimony, for that is established in their books. The true certainty has indeed come to you from your Lord, that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that these Jews and Christians know the truth of that, and find your description in their books, but they deny it despite their knowledge of it. So do not be among those who doubt its truth and reality. The purpose of the verse is to establish the proof against the polytheists through the testimony of the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, in order to cut off their excuse.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 10, verse 95:

"And do not be, O Messenger, among those who denied the proofs and evidences of Allah, lest you be among the losers, those upon whom Allah is angry and who have incurred His punishment."

Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified (O Messenger), by their being expelled from His mercy and by His punishment for them, will not believe in the proofs of Allah, nor acknowledge His oneness, nor act in accordance with His law.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 10, verse 97:

Even if every admonition and lesson came to them, until they witness the painful punishment, then they would believe at that time, but their faith would not benefit them.

This is the commentary on surah 10, verse 98 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

The faith of a people of a town did not benefit them when they believed at the sight of the punishment, except the people of the town of Yunus ibn Matta (Yunus, son of Matta). When they became certain that the punishment was descending upon them, they turned to Allah, the Exalted, with sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhan). When their sincerity in their repentance became clear, Allah removed from them the punishment of disgrace after it had drawn near to them, and He left them in this world to enjoy its benefits until the time their appointed terms (ajal) came to an end.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 99:

And if your Lord had willed, all those on earth would have believed together. So, O Messenger, will you then compel people until they become believers? But He has a wisdom in that: He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, in accordance with His wisdom. And it is not within your capacity to compel people to believe.

No soul could believe except by God's permission and His guidance. So do not exhaust yourself striving for that, for their affair rests with God. God will bring punishment and disgrace upon those who do not use their reason to understand His command and His prohibition.

Say, [O Messenger], to your people: "Reflect and take heed of the signs of God that are in the heavens and the earth, which are clear proofs." But the signs, the lessons, and the messengers warning God's servants of His punishment do not benefit a people who do not believe in any of that, because of their turning away and their obstinacy.

Will these people await anything but a day in which they witness the punishment of Allah, like the days of their predecessors who denied and passed on before them? Say to them, O Messenger: "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."

Then We deliver Our messengers and those who believed along with them. Just as We delivered those (earlier peoples), We shall deliver you, O Messenger, and those who have believed in you, out of Our grace and mercy.

Say, O Messenger, to these people: If you are in doubt about the truth of my religion, which I have called you to, namely Islam, and about my steadfastness and firmness upon it, and you hope to turn me away from it, then I do not worship—under any circumstances—any of those whom you worship, of the idols and images that you have taken. Rather, I worship Allah alone, the One who causes you to die and takes your souls. And I have been commanded to be among those who believe in Him and act according to His law.

And that you should set your face toward the religion, as a upright monotheist (ḥanīf), not inclining away from it toward Judaism, nor Christianity, nor the worship of anything other than Him. And do not be among those who associate partners in the worship of their Lord, the deities and rivals, so that you would be among the ruined. And although this is an address to the Messenger (ﷺ), it is directed to the whole Ummah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 106:

And do not call upon, O Messenger, besides Allah, anything of the idols and images, for they neither benefit nor harm. If you were to do so, calling upon them besides Allah, then you would indeed be among the polytheists who associate others with Allah, and among the wrongdoers against themselves through shirk and disobedience. And although this is an address to the Messenger ﷺ, it is directed to the whole Ummah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 10, verse 107:

﴿And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is none who can remove it except Him. And if He wills good for you, there is none who can repel His bounty.﴾ Say, O Messenger, that if Allah afflicts you with hardship or calamity, none can remove it except Him, may He be exalted and glorified. And if He wills you good, in the form of ease or blessing, no one can prevent it from reaching you. Allah afflicts with comfort and hardship whomever He wills of His servants, and He is the Oft-Forgiving to the sins of those who repent, the Most Merciful to those who believe in Him and obey Him.

Say, [O Messenger], to these people: "The Messenger of God has come to you with the Qur'an, which contains the clarification of your guidance. Whoever is guided by God's guidance, the fruit of his deed returns only to himself; and whoever deviates from the truth and persists in misguidance, his misguidance and harm fall only upon himself. I am not appointed as a guardian over you until you become believers. I am only a messenger who conveys, delivering to you that with which I have been sent."

Follow, O Messenger, the revelation of God that is revealed to you, and act upon it. Be patient in obeying God, in refraining from disobedience to Him, and in bearing the harm inflicted upon you by those who injure you in conveying His message, until God decides His command concerning them and concerning you. He, mighty and majestic, is the best of judges, for His judgment encompasses perfect justice.
